title: ZIA Advanced Threat Protection
aliases: why is this blocked as a threat

global-policy.statement: Advanced Threat Protection is a global policy that applies to all users.

quotes: The Advanced Threat Protection policy is a global policy, so it applies to all users.

no-scoping.statement: There is no per-user, per-group or per-location scope for ATP: each toggle is on or off for the whole tenant, and the API is one settings object plus two URL lists.
no-scoping.conditions: Derived from the policy being global; no source describes a scoping control and none was found in the help page or the API.

before-ips.statement: When a tenant has both Advanced Threat Protection and IPS Control, the rules created for Advanced Threat Protection are evaluated first.

quotes: If you have Advanced Threat Protection as well as IPS Control, any rules you create for Advanced Threat Protection are evaluated first.

recommended-policy.statement: The recommended policy sets Page Risk to 35, blocks everything in Botnet, Malicious Active Content, Fraud, Unauthorized Communication and XSS protection, and blocks BitTorrent, Tor and Google Hangouts.

quotes: Malicious Active Content Protection: Block all

client-connector-notice.statement: When ATP blocks malicious activity matching a user's traffic, Zscaler Client Connector shows a notification that the activity was blocked as potentially harmful.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector displays a notification that the activity was blocked as potentially harmful.

save-and-activate.statement: A change to the policy is saved and then activated in the console.

quotes: Click Save and activate the change.
